title: 'We can feel the RN wave coming': A traditional stronghold of French conservatives shifts right
subhead: 'Europe's far right takes root' (2/6). As the Rassemblement National pursues a meticulous grassroots strategy in the largely rural department of Seine-et-Marne, on the outskirts of Paris, right-leaning voters have been sliding, election after election, toward Marine Le Pen's party.

subhead: The US president devoted part of his self-congratulatory speech on Tuesday to his unpopular military intervention in Iran. 'Do I drive them into hell?' he dangled rhetorically, before suggesting a possible agreement after the midterm elections in November.

title: Ancient wall discovered in Paris, possibly confirming site of city's original settlement
subhead: The stone-and-wood wall, about 20 meters long, was unearthed in the heart of Paris, the Ministry of Culture said. It may be a fragment of the rampart of Lutetia, built by the Gallic Parisii tribe.

title: A veteran of French politics is spicing up the Socialists' primary: Segolène Royal
subhead: Twenty years after losing to Nicolas Sarkozy in the 2007 presidential election, Ségolène Royal is making a new run for the top office. With her campaign struggling to take off, she has started attacking one of the favorites, Raphaël Glucksmann.

title: Emma Heming Willis on her husband Bruce Willis's illness: 'Once I stopped being in denial, we've learned to just navigate the disease'
subhead: The actor learned he was suffering from a neurodegenerative disease at 67. Close to four years after the diagnosis, his wife describes how she coped with the illness and her new role as a caregiver.

title: A$AP Rocky, the rapper reinventing masculinity
subhead: Like many of his peers, the superstar grew up amid poverty and violence. Yet he stands apart in the rap world, rejecting homophobia and misogyny. A Chanel ambassador who embraces being 'Mr. Rihanna', he is both an heir to the tradition of Black dandyism and the embodiment of a masculinity less bound by traditional norms.
